1. Action potential arrives

Ca²⁺ enters the terminal

3. Vesicles fuse with the membrane,
mediator is released by exocytosis

4. Mediator diffuses across the synaptic cleft
(≈0.5 ms synaptic delay)

5. Binds to postsynaptic receptors —
ion channels open
(a) Relationship of whole muscle and muscle fibers

(b) Relationship of
muscle fiber and
myofibrils

2. Myosin head carrying ADP+Pi
binds to actin
(a cross-bridge forms)

3. Phosphate is released — the head
tilts 45°: the “power stroke”,
actin filament slides to the sarcomere centre

4. ADP is released, new ATP binds —
the head detaches from actin

While Ca²⁺ is present,
the cycle repeats

Without ATP —
the head stays bound to actin:
rigor mortis

5. ATP is hydrolysed —
the head is “cocked”
(returns to the starting position)

Thermoreceptors:
skin (mostly cold), internal organs,
thermosensitive hypothalamic neurons

IN COLD: heat conservation
• skin vessels constrict
• piloerection
• sweating stops

IN COLD: heat production
• shivering
• non-shivering thermogenesis
(brown fat, thyroxine, adrenaline)

IN HEAT: heat loss
• skin vessels dilate
• sweating (evaporation)
• panting (in animals)

IN HEAT: reduced heat
production
(lethargy, reduced appetite)
